member.name: T:Prowl.Prism.Compiler.PreciseAnalysis
member.summary:
glslang's PropagateNoContraction (propagateNoContraction.cpp), over Prism's AST: starting from every assignment to a precise object, walks backwards through the assignments of every object its value depends on (call arguments, constructor arguments and ternary conditions included, index expressions not), and marks the arithmetic operations involved. member.name: T:Prowl.Prism.Optimizer.SpirVOptimizer
member.summary:
Post-lowering optimizer. Takes the straight-lowered SPIR-V word stream and returns an optimized one, targeting byte-for-byte parity with spirv-opt's Performance pipeline (the level shaderc runs at OptimizationLevel.Performance).
Phase 2 adds passes here one at a time, in spirv-opt's order. Until the pipeline reproduces every transformation for a given module, its optimized parity test stays red and marks what is left to do.
The full, verified feature-gap list (front-end AND optimizer) lives in /GAPS.md at the repo root. Passes present here: StripDebug, DeadBranchElim, MergeReturn, Inline(=InlineExhaustive, O(n)), EliminateDeadFunctions, PrivateToLocal, LocalSingleBlockElim, LocalSingleStoreElim, ScalarReplacement, LocalAccessChainConvert, SsaRewrite(=LocalMultiStoreElim), GlobalCse(=RedundancyElimination), RedundantLoadElim, BlockMerge, RecomputeBound. ReciprocalFDiv and FoldInsertWithConstants are folding rules inside Simplification/Ccp. The dominant remaining blocker is NOT missing capability -- it is byte-parity: matching spirv-opt's exact scratch/throwaway id-allocation and fold ORDER. Nearly every remaining red is functionally correct + valid.

member.name: T:Prowl.Prism.Optimizer.Folder
member.summary:
A faithful port of spirv-opt's shared folding engine: the ConstantManager (constants.cpp), the InstructionFolder dispatch (fold.cpp), and const_folding_rules.cpp. CCP and the Simplification pass both go through this, so the constants it materializes get their ids in exactly spirv-opt's order -- byte parity by construction, instead of two separate approximations (the old inline CCP folder and SimplifyFolds).
A "constant" is identified by its defining instruction (OpConstant / OpConstantTrue|False / OpConstantNull / OpConstantComposite). Constants are created lazily and deduped by value, and appended to the types/constants section (before the first OpFunction) with a fresh id from Header[3] -- matching ConstantManager:: GetDefiningInstruction -> FindDeclaredConstant / BuildInstructionAndAddToModule.
